newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent edges up but downside still beckons.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent edges up but downside still beckons.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures edged tentatively higher in early trading on Thursday after losing ground over the past couple of days.
July was up four cents at $18.76 a barrel at 0933 GMT but remained in contango some 16 cents below August.
Dealers said the market looked technically weak with support at $18.65 and $18.50 and some see a soggy outlook in the physical market.
There were plenty of physical Brent cargoes still unsold in June and dealers expected higher output in July when some North Sea fields resume production after maintenance.
There was little fresh news affecting the market on Thursday after Wednesday's renewal of Iraq's oil for food deal.
Dealers said U.S. gasoline demand was failing to lift the wider market and many expected the weight of other oil products in the West to soon pressure crude prices.
"Keep an eye on products as they are main still negative and could therefore lead us lower," said Mees Pierson Derivatives in London.
IPE gas oil was down 25 cents a tonne at $168.50 at 0927 GMT but analysts saw robust technical support in the area $160.00 to $165.00 a widely traded range in April.
Physical markets remained little changed at $1.25 a tonne above the screen for Rotterdam barges but dealers say inland demand from German remains sluggish.
